## Issues

### ISSUE-0001 [Open] Trace map is not an isomorphism onto the finite/cofinite algebra
- **Category:** Supplement/remark error
- **Location:** supplement (高い視点から)
- **Detail:** The supplement claims that the trace map is an isomorphism from the Lindenbaum algebra of GL-equivalence classes of letterless formulas onto the Boolean algebra of finite/cofinite subsets of N enriched with X↦{n:[0,n)⊂X}. This is false: the Lindenbaum algebra of GL is countable, whereas the algebra of finite/cofinite subsets of N is countably infinite, so cardinality alone does not refute it, but the real problem is that the claimed algebra is not closed under the operation in the way stated and, more importantly, the map is not injective on the intended structure: distinct GL-equivalence classes can have the same trace only if provably equivalent, which is fine, but the 'algebra' generated by the operation X↦{n:[0,n)⊂X} applied to finite/cofinite sets is not the stated set. Concretely, applying the box operation to a cofinite set gives a finite initial segment, and the resulting structure is not a Boolean algebra closed under the box; the claim that the trace map is an isomorphism onto 'this algebra' is imprecise/overstated. The correct statement is only that the trace map induces an injective Boolean homomorphism (embedding) from the Lindenbaum algebra into the finite/cofinite Boolean algebra, and that it is surjective onto finite/cofinite sets, hence a Boolean isomorphism onto the finite/cofinite algebra, but the box operation is not part of the Boolean signature and the 'algebra with the added operation' is not a Boolean algebra in the usual sense.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the claim with: 'The trace map induces a Boolean algebra isomorphism from the Lindenbaum algebra of letterless formulas (modulo GL-provability) onto the Boolean algebra of finite or cofinite subsets of N (injectivity by \ref{pt:trace-provability}, surjectivity by \ref{pt:normal-form-by-trace}). The modality corresponds under this isomorphism to the map X↦{n:[0,n)⊂X}, which sends finite/cofinite sets to finite/cofinite sets, but this map is not a Boolean algebra operation, so one should speak of an isomorphism of Boolean algebras compatible with the modality, not of an isomorphism onto an algebra with the box adjoined.'
- **Reported:** 2026-10-28 (8ccef3d)

### ISSUE-0002 [Open] Claim that the same proof works for any T with D1–D3 and formalized Löb is too strong
- **Category:** Supplement/remark error
- **Location:** supplement (前提の検討, third bullet)
- **Detail:** The supplement asserts that replacing PA by any recursively axiomatized theory T true in N with D1–D3 and the formalized Löb theorem gives the same proof. But \ref{pt:box-bot-false} uses not only D1–D3 and Löb but also that T is sound in N (N⊨T) and that Bew correctly represents provability (\ref{pt:bew-correct}); moreover \ref{pt:letterless-gl-pa} uses the arithmetical soundness of GL for T, which requires that the provability predicate for T satisfies the Hilbert–Bernays–Löb derivability conditions AND that T proves the corresponding reflection instances used. The statement 'the same proof goes through' is stated more strongly than warranted: one must additionally require that T is Σ_{1}-sound (or at least that Bew_{T} satisfies the correct provability conditions and that T is consistent enough for Löb), and that the formalized Löb theorem holds for T. The parenthetical hedge does not repair the overstatement.
- **Proposed fix:** Weaken to: 'The same argument goes through for any recursively axiomatized theory T true in N whose provability predicate satisfies D1–D3 and the formalized Löb theorem, and for which the arithmetical soundness of GL (\ref{pt:gl-arithmetical-soundness}) holds; in particular T must be Σ_{1}-sound so that \ref{pt:bew-correct} applies.'
- **Reported:** 2026-10-28 (8ccef3d)
